tools.name: generate_qr_code
tools.title: Generate a QR code
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a new QR code that is also a picture: a scannable code painted into art from a description, that opens a link. It starts the code and answers at once with its id while the picture is painted, which usually takes under a minute; then call get_qr_code with the id to wait for the image. Do not use it to look at, list or change codes that already exist. Each code counts against the user’s QRX allowance.

prompt.description: What the picture should show, e.g. "a lighthouse on a cliff at sunset".

destination.description: The link scans open: an absolute http or https URL, e.g. https://example.com/menu.

style.description: A style id from list_styles. Leave out for the default.

id.description: The code’s id. A link code’s id is also the path of its short link: lowercase letters and digits, currently 6 characters. A Wi-Fi code’s id is a UUID. Treat every id as an opaque, case-sensitive string of up to 64 characters. It never changes.

status.description: `processing` until the picture is painted and checked to scan; then `succeeded` or `failed`. `queued` is reserved for a code waiting to start. More values may be added: treat anything other than `succeeded` or `failed` as still in progress.

type.description: `url` for a link code, `wifi` for a Wi-Fi code. More values may be added.

style.description: The style id, if one was chosen.

destination.description: Where a link code’s scans go; null for a Wi-Fi code.

wifi.description: The network a Wi-Fi code joins; null for a link code. The password is never returned.

security.description: More values (such as `nopass`) may be added.

shortUrl.description: The link the code encodes (`https://qrx.to/<id>`); scans go through it to `destination`. Null for a Wi-Fi code.

imageUrl.description: The finished image (PNG), once the code has succeeded.

pageUrl.description: The code’s page in the app.

error.description: Why the code failed, when it did.

completedAt.description: When the code succeeded or failed; null while it is processing.

derivedFrom.description: Set on a variation (`POST /v1/codes/{id}/variations`): the code it was made from and the change; null otherwise.

id.description: The id of the code it was made from.

change.description: The change that was asked for.

method.description: `edit`: the original’s picture was changed. `redraw`: the original was made before QRX kept pictures, so the variation was drawn again from its prompt with the change. More values may be added.

tools.name: generate_qr_code_from_image
tools.title: Generate a QR code from an image
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a scannable QR code woven into a picture they already have (a photo, an illustration or artwork) instead of one painted from a description. Pass the picture once, as exactly one of an attached file (image), a public https link (imageUrl) or base64 (imageBase64): PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 10 MB and at least 256 pixels on each side; the code uses its centre square. Every picture is checked for safety first, and one that does not pass is refused with an error and nothing is made. It starts the code and answers at once with its id while it is painted, which usually takes under a minute; then call get_qr_code with the id to wait for the image. Do not use it to look at, list or change codes that already exist. Each code counts against the user’s QRX allowance.

prompt.description: Optional: what the picture shows, to guide how it is redrawn. Leave out to have it described automatically.

tools.name: vary_qr_code
tools.title: Make a variation of a QR code
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a new QR code based on one of their existing codes, with a change to its picture, e.g. "more trees" or "make it night time". It makes a new code with its own id and short link that opens the same destination and keeps the original’s style and logo; the original code does not change. It answers at once with the new code’s id while the picture is painted; then call get_qr_code with the id to wait for the image. Only link codes the user owns can be varied. Do not use it to change where a code points or to make an unrelated code. Each variation counts against the user’s QRX allowance.

tools.name: get_account
tools.title: Get plan and usage
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how many QR codes they can still make today, when the daily count resets, or what their QRX account can do. Do not use it to make or list codes.

plan.description: What the account pays for. `features` says what it can do today, and the two can differ (for QRX staff, say), so act on `features`. More values may be added.

codes.description: The daily allowance. All null when the account has no daily limit.

prefix.description: The start of the API key, enough to tell keys apart.

environment.description: The QRX site the credentials work on: `live` on qrx.codes. More values may be added.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: Get the signed-in QRX account
tools.description: Use this when you need to know which QRX account is connected, for example to confirm it with the user. Do not use it for limits; use get_account.

tools.name: list_styles
tools.title: List QR code styles
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to choose a look for a new QR code; pass a style id to generate_qr_code. Do not use it to make a code.
